🧊🧭CALL FOR PROPOSALS | Participation in China's 43rd Antarctic Expedition (2026–2027) | Hong Kong Polar Science Innovation Centre (HKPSIC)  - Hong Kong Polar Science Innovation Centre
From: Yolanda YIM
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
yolandayim@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
An Opportunity to Conduct Research in Antarctica
________________________________________________________________________________________________
The Hong Kong Polar Science Innovation Centre (HKPSIC) is pleased to invite proposals from scientists and researchers interested in participating in
China’s 43rd Antarctic Expedition (2026–2027)
.
Research opportunities are available at
Great Wall Station
and
Zhongshan Station
in Antarctica. All proposals and personnel nominations will be reviewed and selected by the Polar Research Institute of China (PRIC).
This opportunity is primarily open to researchers from universities in Hong Kong.
Expedition Purpose
The expedition will be conducted for
scientific research purposes
.
Research Opportunities
Great Wall Station (Antarctica)
Quota:
Tentatively 2–5 participants
(Subject to adjustment based on the approved research proposals.)
Eligibility:
Undergraduate students
Postgraduate students
PhD candidates
Postdoctoral fellows
Academic staff and researchers
For student participation, it is recommended that faculty members form research teams with their students.
Duration:
Approximately 2–4 weeks at the station
Entry via Punta Arenas, Chile
Tentative departure between late December 2026 and January 2027 or January to February 2027
Additional travel time should be allowed for international flights
Zhongshan Station (Antarctica)
Quota:
1–2 participant(s)
Eligibility:
Postdoctoral fellows or above
Students are not eligible
Duration:
Approximately 2–4 months at the station
Tentative departure from Australia aboard the icebreaker
Xuelong
or
Xuelong 2
in November 2026
Return to Shanghai in April 2027
Additional travel time should be allowed for flights to Australia and from Shanghai
Research Instruments
As the icebreakers
Xuelong
and
Xuelong 2
will depart from Shanghai, PRIC recommends that any required research instruments be shipped to Shanghai no later than
mid-October 2026
for loading and transportation to the Antarctic research stations.
Health and Visa Requirements
Selected participants will be required to:
Complete a medical examination specified by PRIC
Submit a medical report for review
Obtain visas for Chile and/or Australia (if applicable)
Participants should allow sufficient time for medical examinations and visa applications.
Clothing and Equipment
PRIC will provide basic expedition clothing and equipment, including:
Expedition jackets
Trousers
Thermal wear
Sunglasses
Other essential gear
These items will be provided to selected participants before departure.
Expenses to Be Covered by Participants
Participants are responsible for all associated expenses, including:
International airfares
Round-trip flights between Punta Arenas and Great Wall Station
(approximately USD 4,000 per person)
Accommodation before and after station entry/exit
(Accommodation at Antarctic research stations is provided free of charge)
Travel insurance
Visa application fees (if applicable)
Medical examination fees
Shipment and transportation costs for research instruments and equipment
Any other incidental expenses
Proposal Submission
Researchers who are able to meet the above requirements and schedule are invited to submit an email request to obtain the proposal template.
Submission Deadline
4 August 2026 (Tuesday)
All proposals will be forwarded to PRIC for evaluation and selection. HKPSIC will provide support to participating researchers and facilitate communications with PRIC throughout the application and preparation process.
Enquiries
Secretariat
Hong Kong Polar Science Innovation Centre (HKPSIC)
Email: hkpsic@cuhk.edu.hk
Tel: 3943 0345
We sincerely encourage interested researchers to take advantage of this unique opportunity to conduct scientific research in Antarctica and contribute to polar research collaboration.
We look forward to receiving your proposals.
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
/weekly/

The Learning and Cultural Enhancement Section of the Office of Student Affairs is committed to offering students guidance on adjustment to and planning for university life and to promoting cultural interchange on campus.
We are recruiting student helpers to provide on-site support for a series of activities for students in August and September 2026.
Please refer to the application form for details and indicate your preferred position(s) and availability.
Available Positions:
Roles
Date
1
Guided Library Tour for Postgraduate New Students
7, 25, 31 August 2026
2
Event Support and Campus Tour @ Meet-and-Greet Days/ Postgraduate Welcoming Day
28 August 2026
3
Photography @ Meet-and-Greet Days/ Postgraduate Welcoming Day
28 August 2026
4
Videography (IG Reels for snapshots & student interviews) @ University Orientation Day and Meet-and-Greet Days/ Postgraduate Welcoming Day
6, 28 August 2026
5
Support for i-House Mass Check-in/out
31 August, 5 & 6 September 2026
[Remarks: For Positions 3 & 4, additional hours will be granted for photo editing & video production before and/or beyond the event.]
Helper Fees:
HKD 64/hour (plus a 5% Mandatory Provident Fund contribution) on or before 31 August 2026
HKD 67/hour (plus a 5% Mandatory Provident Fund contribution) starting from 1 September 2026
Requirements:
Applicants are expected to possess the following qualifications, experience, and attributes:
·         Current full-time undergraduate or postgraduate students
·         Good communication skills in English, Cantonese, and Putonghua
·         Sincere, polite, and responsible attitude
·         Proactive and willing to serve the CUHK community
Application:
Interested students please fill out the
application form
by
24 Jul 2026 (Fri).
Being a student helper not only allows you to contribute to the vibrant campus community, but it also provides valuable experience in event planning, customer service, and teamwork. We look forward to working with you this summer!

.

From: Tang Tsz Chung
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
tctang@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
【誠邀出席】網絡研討會｜生命最後的安寧：殘疾人士在居處離世的選擇
在生命最後的階段，殘疾人士除了在醫院離世，在可行條件下，能夠選擇在居處安寧離世——無論在院舍或在家，這樣的安排使他們在熟悉的環境中獲得尊重與安寧，亦有機會表達自己的意願。
這次研討會透過探討「在居處離世」的選擇，讓大家更認識相關方案，並了解如何支援殘疾人士在生命最後階段作出決定。透過溝通與交流，共建在居處離世的理解與尊重。❤️💕
✨
研討會內容：
① 什麼是「在居處離世」及常見迷思
② 在居處善終的考量與準備
③ 如何支援殘疾人士表達安寧照顧選擇與意願
④ 個案分享及互動問答環節
⑤ 問答環節
📅

日期：2026年8月5日 （星期三）
時間：下午 12:30 -  2:00
形式：Zoom 線上直播（費用全免）

對象：公眾人士
語言：廣東話

[Invitation] Webinar | Peace at Journey's End: 'Dying in Place' Options for Persons with Disabilities
In the final stages of life, besides hospital care, Persons with Disabilities (PWDs) can also choose to pass away peacefully in their place of residence under feasible circumstances. Whether in a residential care home or at home, such an arrangement allows them to receive respect and tranquility in a familiar environment, while granting them the precious opportunity to express their own wishes.
By exploring the options of "Dying in Place," this webinar aims to enhance public understanding of relevant pathways and discuss how to support PWDs in making informed decisions during their final journey. Through meaningful communication and exchange, let us together foster understanding and respect for dying in place. ❤️💕
✨ Webinar Highlights:
① Introduction to 'Dying in Place' & Common Myths
② Practical Requirements, Considerations, and Preparations
③ Facilitating and Supporting PWDs to Express Their Palliative Care Choices & Wishes
④ Local Case Sharing
⑤ Q&A Session

Counselling, caring, listening and sharing - Community Support Counseling
The Professional Educational Psychology and Counselling Service of the Department of Educational Psychology of The Chinese University of Hong Kong hopes to help people in need to explore their problems, understand their own thoughts and feelings, and make appropriate choices and actions. Counsellor trainees who are receiving training from our master’s level counselling program will provide Zoom or face-to-face counselling services. The counselling service will be conducted from Jul to Dec 2026. Each session is 50 minutes, and the cost per session is HK$100. For those with low income, each session is HK$30. Services are limited, if you are looking for counselling (non-urgent cases), please register by filling out the application form below.
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=6411435
For more service details, please call 3943 3413 or email pepcs@cuhk.edu.hk, we will reply you during office hours, thank you.

bodyText:

Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/07/17
»
Announcements
👩🥰 Recruiting Post-Menopausal Women with Elevated/Stage I Hypertension for Participation in a Ten-Week Oral NR Supplementation (Market Value: 4200 HKD) and Aerobic Exercise Study :D 招募停經後且患有血壓偏高/第一期高血壓女性參與為期十週的NR補充劑 (市場價值: 4200 HKD) 與有氧運動研究 - Department of Sports Science & Physical Education; Program Director: Prof. Stephen Heung-sang WONG
From: ZHANG Jiaqi
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
1155189512@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
儘管已有指導方針規定的藥物治療方案，高血壓在全球範圍內仍然非常普遍，並且是心血管疾病的主要風險因素。 在中國，約三分之一的成年人患有高血壓，但控制良好的血壓患者比例不到 5%。特別是停經後女性， 由於年齡增長和更年期過渡的綜合影響，患高血壓的風險顯著增加。最近的研究表明，恢復 NAD 水平可能是一種治療方法，能夠改善內皮功能並減輕高血壓患者的血管功能障礙。 NAD 是人體內最重要的分子之一，在調節主要生物過程中起著關鍵作用，並會隨著年齡增長而下降。因此，本隨機對照試驗的目的是通過口服 NR 補充劑和/或有氧運動來研究提升 NAD 水平是否能改善血壓升高/高血壓一期的停經後女性的高血壓症狀。 參與本研究，您將有機會獲得市值 4,200 港元的 NR 補充劑及參與專業指導的運動班。所有研究相關費用均由研究團隊承擔，您無需支付任何費用。本研究不設額外物質或金錢獎勵。
🙌🙌
參與資格：
停經超過一年；
華裔；
符合《2025 年美國心臟病學會/美國心臟協會成人高血壓預防、檢測、評估與管理指南》中對血壓升高/高血壓一期的標準（即血壓≥120/80 mmHg 且 <140/90 mmHg，基於≥2 次測量的平均值）；
無運動習慣。
🙅‍♀️🙅‍♀️
排除標准：
存在不適合參加運動訓練的健康狀況；
子宮切除病史；
正在食用維生素B或NAD補充劑。
🙌🙌
參加方法：
點擊海報或通過以下鏈接作網上登記【
https://forms.gle/ggPtpRDCdes3xuhE8
】；
研究團隊會進行初步篩選，以了解您是否符合基本參加資格；
成功通過初步篩選後，預約檢查時間；
前往香港中文大學汾陽體育館參加檢查；
如果符合參加條件，將會被隨機分組，正式開展後續正式的研究計劃。
🙌🙌
計劃內容：
隨機分組：急步行結合 NR 補充劑組 (NRBW)；急步行結合安慰劑組 (PLBW)；僅使用 NR 補充劑組 (NR)；僅使用安慰劑組 (PL)；
10星期 NR補充劑/有氧運動（根據隨機分組後的內容）；

Despite guideline-recommended pharmacological treatment strategies, hypertension remains highly prevalent worldwide and is a major risk factor for cardiovascular disease. In China, approximately one-third of adults have hypertension, yet fewer than 5% achieve well-controlled blood pressure. Postmenopausal women, in particular, face a significantly increased risk of developing hypertension due to the combined effects of aging and the menopausal transition.
Recent research suggests that restoring NAD levels may serve as a therapeutic approach to improve endothelial function and alleviate vascular dysfunction in individuals with hypertension. NAD is one of the most important molecules in the human body, playing a critical role in regulating major biological processes, and its levels decline with age. Therefore, this randomized controlled trial aims to investigate whether increasing NAD levels through oral nicotinamide riboside (NR) supplementation and/or aerobic exercise can improve hypertension symptoms in postmenopausal women with elevated blood pressure or Stage I hypertension.
Participation in this study is free of charge. You will not need to pay for any study-related items or services, and no material compensation (including monetary incentives) will be provided.

Chinese;

Better Gut, Better Sleep? Gut-Brain Study | 💰🎁 Earn up to HKD 500 「腸」通無阻，瞓得更好？「腸·腦」研究 | 💰🎁最高可獲 HKD 500 - Department of Psychiatry
From: Jephthah Cheung
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
lokcheung@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
近年醫學界發現，我們的腸道健康與大腦息息相關！原來「便秘」和「睡眠質素」的改變，可能是腦部退化的早期信號。為了深入了解這條神奇的「腸腦連線」，香港中文大學精神科學系睡眠研究組現正招募研究參加者。
研究對象:
年齡介乎 50 至 80 歲
關注腸道健康或者受便秘問題困擾（如排便困難、次數較少等）
沒有腦退化、精神疾病史
參加者需完成以下簡單程序：
填寫問卷 及 進行簡單面談
進行一次非入侵性睡眠檢測
記錄連續兩星期「大便日記」
進行一次結腸運輸試驗
收集一次大便樣本
參與研究費用全免，成功參與者最多可獲 HKD 500 超市禮券的津貼
如對本研究有興趣，請透過以下連結報名參加：
[網址連結:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_eeTcY6hrKILNwhg
]
如對研究內容有任何疑問，歡迎致電 📞 3919 7792 / 9568 9006 或 📱 WhatsApp 9568 9006與負責研究人員聯絡、查詢詳情。謝謝🙏🏻
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Recent research suggests that gut health is closely linked to brain function. Changes in bowel habits (e.g. constipation) and sleep quality may even be early signs of neurodegeneration.
To better understand this “gut–brain axis, we sincerely invite you to take part in our research study.
Who can join:
Aged 50–80
Concerned about gut health or bothered by constipation
No history of dementia or psychiatric disorders
What you will do:
Complete questionnaires and a brief interview
Undergo a sleep assessment
Record a 2-week bowel diary
Complete a colonic transit time test
Collect one stool sample
Incentive:
All assessments are free of charge.
Eligible participants may receive up to HKD 500 in supermarket vouchers upon completion.
Interested? Please sign up here:
[
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_eeTcY6hrKILNwhg
]
Enquiries:
📞 3919 7792 / 9568 9006
📱 WhatsApp 9568 9006
View Count

https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

Recruitment: Student Helper
Position Description:
The Infectious Disease Research Team at the Department of Medicine & Therapeutics, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, cordially invites CUHK students to join our clinical vaccine trial support work! Our team is led by experienced medical professionals dedicated to clinical research. We are recruiting student helpers to participate in important clinical preparation work before and after vaccination. Under our guidance, you will gain valuable hands-on experience in clinical research, learning while working and experiencing the real value and significance of scientific research first hand. Work is based at Prince of Wales Hospital in a comfortable, relaxed environment with no fieldwork required—an ideal internship platform.
Responsibilities:
Pre-trial preparations (e.g., sample container labelling, document organization, material setup)
Assist with biological sample and data collection before/after vaccination when needed
Perform clinical research tasks assigned by research supervisor
Requirements:
CUHK undergraduate or postgraduate student
Available for at least one session per week, minimum 3-4 hours per session (flexible scheduling, to be arranged with supervisor, working hours to be adjusted based on subsequent research workload and needs)
Responsible, detail-oriented, and reliable
Proficient in English and Chinese.
Preferred Qualifications:
Science, medicine, nursing, pharmacy or related fields preferred; other disciplines also welcome
Interest in clinical research or vaccine trials
Salary: HKD$64 / hour
Application:
Please email your CV to catherinecheung@cuhk.edu.hk
Applications welcome immediately!

實驗時間：
需來两次：一節爲腦電實驗，約3小時；一節爲行為實驗，約2.5小時。
實驗內容：
①腦電實驗：
佩戴腦電帽
（對人體安全無害）完成語言學習任務
腦電實驗中，您將會接受
經顱光生物調節（tPBM）
：此儀器用一束微弱的光刺激額頭，同樣對人體完全無害，不會有任何感覺，已獲得大學和醫院的使用批准，這種儀器已被證實可以有效提高記憶力。
②行為實驗：完成一系列語言和認知測試；
③填寫問卷。
實驗地點：①腦電/光調節實驗在香港中文大學王福元樓406A進行；②行為實驗在香港中文大學梁銶琚樓G/F進行
兩次實驗結束後，會支付500港元被試費用。
參與者需要符合以下要求：
1. 年齡18-30歲，非心理學/語言學專業。
2. 母語為廣東話；
3. 聽力、視力或矯正視力正常；
4. 無腦損傷、癲癇等神經類疾病，無頭皮外傷或感染；
5. 右利手；
6. 實驗時間身體健康，無感冒發燒咳嗽等狀況；
7. 實驗前要保證充足的睡眠，精力充沛認真負責完成實驗；
8. 實驗前24小時未服用大量茶、咖啡等飲料；實驗前不要有劇烈的體育活動；
9. 實驗前兩週不能染髮；
10. 實驗當天需要洗頭，不能化妝，額頭不要塗防曬霜、隔離霜等。
如有任何問題，請聯繫：xinwen.chen@cuhk.edu.hk
⚠️報名連結🔗：
http://137.189.158.12/limesurvey/index.php?r=survey/index&sid=813414&lang=zh-Hant-HK
Experiment Duration:
You will need to visit twice: one session for the EEG experiment (approximately 3 hours) and one session for the behavioral experiment (approximately 2.5 hours).
Experiment Details:
1. EEG experiment: Completing language learning tasks with an
EEG
cap
Participants in the EEG study will receive
transcranial photobiomodulation (tPBM)
: This device uses a weak beam of light to stimulate the forehead. It is completely harmless to the human body and causes no sensation. This type of device has been proven to effectively improve memory and has been approved for use by universities and hospitals.
2. Behavioral experiment: Completing a series of language and cognitive tests;
3. Completion of questionnaires.
Experiment Locations: 406A, Wong Foo Yuan Building OR G/F, Leung Kau Kui Building, CUHK
After completing
both sessions
, participants will receive a reimbursement of
HK$500
.
Eligibility Requirements:
Aged 18–30; not majoring in psychology or linguistics.
Cantonese native speaker.
Normal hearing and vision, or corrected-to-normal vision.
No history of brain injury, epilepsy, or other neurological conditions; no scalp injuries or infections.
Right-handed (i.e., habitually writes or uses chopsticks with the right hand).
In good health on the day of the experiment (no cold, fever, cough, etc.).
Well-rested before the experiment, and able to complete the task attentively and responsibly.
No consumption of large amounts of tea, coffee, or similar drinks within 24 hours prior; no intense physical activity before the experiment.
No hair dyeing within two weeks before the experiment.
Please wash your hair and do not wear makeup or apply sunscreen/primer/foundation on the forehead on the day of the experiment.
For inquiries, please contact: xinwen.chen@cuhk.edu.hk

研究計劃，目的旨在開發和驗證適合香港情況的跨專業教育干預措施，為政府的衛生保健策略提供資訊，以加强慢性病管理。

Centre for Learning Enhancement And Research – CLEAR, The Chinese University of Hong Kong is recruiting individuals with Type 2 diabetes mellitus to participate in a study
【
Interprofessional Self Determination theory-based educational interventions on diabetes mellitus
ma
nagement

.

Announcements
Recurit markers for PIRLS Chinese Reading Assessment PIRLS 2026招募閱卷員 - EdDataX Research Centre
From: Angus NG
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
angusmingho@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
PIRLS 2026 Marker Recruitment
We are delighted to collaborate with the Hong Kong Examinations and Assessment Authority (HKEAA) in conducting
PIRLS
, one of the world's most prestigious international education assessments.
About PIRLS
PIRLS (Progress in International Reading Literacy Study)
is a worldwide research programme that assesses the reading literacy of Primary 4 students and compares educational outcomes across participating countries and regions. Through PIRLS, we gain valuable insights into students' reading performance and provide important evidence to inform educational policy and practice.
Benefits of Becoming a PIRLS Marker
Gain Valuable Professional Experience
Participate in an international educational study and develop a deeper understanding of reading assessment standards and marking methodologies.
Broaden Your Professional Horizons
Exchange ideas with educators from diverse backgrounds and enhance your professional knowledge and skills.
Requirements
Currently pursuing, or holding, a Bachelor's degree in Chinese Language, a Postgraduate Diploma in Education (PGDE), or equivalent qualifications.
Passionate about reading education and assessment, with strong attention to detail and patience.
Responsibilities
Mark students' responses strictly in accordance with the scoring guidelines established by the International Association for the Evaluation of Educational Achievement (IEA).
Work under the guidance of Team Leaders to ensure scoring consistency and accuracy.
Marking Dates and Venue
Dates:
29 July – 7 August 2026
Depending on individual availability, markers will be assigned
2 to 5 working days
. Successful applicants will be notified of their assigned work dates on or before
17 July 2026
.
Working Hours:
10:00 a.m. – 5:00 p.m. (Lunch break: 1:00 p.m. – 2:00 p.m.)
Venue:
HKEAA Hung Hom Office
Remuneration
HK$1,514 per day
Application
If you are interested in joining our team, please complete the online application form:
https://forms.office.com/r/JetCaszPJ5
Application Deadline
17 July 2026
Enquiries
For enquiries, please contact us at
3943 5350
or
3628 8513
.
We look forward to welcoming you to the PIRLS marking team.
本中心很高興能與香港考試及評核局（HKEAA）合作，負責舉辦一項極具權威的全球教育評估——「PIRLS」。
關於
PIRLS
PIRLS（Progress in International Reading Literacy Study，全球學生閱讀能力進展研究）是一項全球性的研究計劃，旨在評估小學四年級學生的閱讀能力，並比較不同國家及地區的教育成效。透過PIRLS，我們能夠深入了解學生的閱讀表現，並為教育政策的制定提供重要參考。
成為
PIRLS
閱卷員的好處
豐富專業經驗
：參與國際性教育研究，深入了解閱讀評估的標準與方法。
拓展視野
：與來自不同背景的教育工作者交流，提升專業能力。
要求
現正修讀或持有中文學士學位／PGDE／學生。
對閱讀教育及評估工作有熱誠，具備細心、耐心的特質。
職責
根據國際教育成就評價協會（IEA）的要求，嚴格按照評分標準進行閱卷。
在閱卷組長的指導下，確保評分的一致性與準確性。
閱卷
日期及地點
日期：2026年7月29日至8月7日
（我們將視乎閱卷員的時間安排二至五天的工作，並會在7月17日前通知成功取錄的閱卷員及工作日期）
時閒：上午 10 時至下午5時 (午飯時間：下午1時- 2時)
地點：香港考試及評核局紅磡辦公室
薪酬
每日薪酬為港幣$1,514。
如有興趣加入我們的團隊，請填寫以下表格：
https://forms.office.com/r/JetCaszPJ5
。
截止申請日期為2026年7月17日。
如有任何查詢，歡迎隨時致電 3943 5350/3628 8513。
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
/weekly/

Announcements
【💫💫💫Earn HK$500 coupon💫💫💫】 Recruiting adults (aged 18-65) to participate in research on online therapy for insomnia🙌🙌🙌 【💫💫💫可獲得 500元現金券💫💫💫】招募成年人 (18-65歲)參與失眠的數碼化治療研究🙌🙌🙌 - Psychiatry
From: Charis
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
mastersleep@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
你是否經常在床上輾轉難眠，夜醒或早醒？你並不孤單——許多人都面臨著同樣的問題。我們誠邀您參與研究，讓專業數碼化治療助你改善睡眠！
研究目的
本研究旨在評估市民對數碼化失眠認知行為治療聊天機器人的遵從性，以及其對改善睡眠問題的效果。
治療方式
· 由專業臨床心理學家及精神科醫生設計的電子化治療
· 完全免費
參與資格
· 18至65歲能說廣東話流利溝通（能流利閱讀並理解廣東話）的香港居民
· 在過去一個月內，每週至少三晚出現睡眠困擾
· 最近四周或以上無需長期服藥
參與研究，獲得獎勵！
完成所有治療及後續測試後，您可獲得高達500港幣。
如何加入？
請點擊以下連結進行註冊，並回答幾條簡單問題。研究員將聯絡適合的參加者，詳細解釋研究內容：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4UPFh054GtJGXX0
聯絡我們
如有任何疑問，請於辦公時間內致電 6115-0322 與研究助理聯絡。
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Do you often toss and turn in bed, wake up frequently at night, or wake up too early? You are not alone—many people experience the same challenges. We invite you to participate in our study and explore professional digital treatment to improve your sleep!
Purpose of the Study
This research aims to evaluate the public’s adherence to a digital insomnia cognitive behavioural therapy chatbot and assess its effectiveness in improving sleep problems.
Treatment Method
· A professionally designed digital therapy created by clinical psychologists and psychiatrists
· Completely free of charge
Eligibility Criteria
· Hong Kong residents aged 18 to 65 who can speak in Cantonese fluently, read and understand Cantonese
· Experienced sleep disturbances at least 3 nights per week in the past month
· No need for long-term medication for the past four weeks or more.
Receive Rewards for Participating!
Upon completion of all treatment sessions and follow-up assessments, participants will receive up to HKD 500.
How to Join?
Click the link below to register and answer a few simple questions. Our researchers will contact suitable participants to provide further details:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4UPFh054GtJGXX0
Contact Us
If you have any questions, please call 6115-0322 during office hours to speak with our research assistants.
View Count

https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

Events / Activities
*Prostate Health Screening* 💥免費前列腺健康篩查－誠邀合資格男士參加💥 - S.H. Ho Urology Centre, Department of Surgery
From: Yellow Wong
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
yellowwong@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
根據衛生署數據，前列腺癌是本港男性常見的癌症之一。透過及早篩查，可以有效降低相關的健康風險。本次活動由中大何善衡泌尿中心舉辦，為合資格人士提供免費的前列腺特異抗原 (PSA) 檢測服務。
活動地點： 沙田區（詳細地址將於成功報名後通知）
活動內容：(所需時間約一小時)
1. 影片講解：深入淺出地介紹前列腺增生及前列腺癌的檢查與治療知識。
2. 前列腺篩查：合資格人士可獲免費前列腺特異抗原（PSA）測試乙次.
• 測試方式：我們將以指尖採血方式為參加者抽取血液樣本，並透過PSA檢測機進行現場測試，約十分鐘即可得知結果。
參加資格：
• 性別：男性
• 年齡：50-75歲
• 從未接受前列腺相關檢查
如有興趣參加活動，請填妥以下表格。
https://forms.office.com/r/HRJspBWSW6
如想了解更多關於前列腺癌風險的評估, 可瀏覽以下網址;
https://urologycentre.com.hk/zh-hant/diseases/detail/how-to-investigate-and-make-diagnosis-for-prostate-cance
r
參加者提供的所有資料將會被保密。如有任何查詢，請與我們聯絡 （Whatsapp: 5160 6904；電郵：yellowwong@cuhk.edu.hk）。
According to data from the Department of Health, prostate cancer is one of the most common cancers among men in Hong Kong. Early screening can effectively reduce related health risks. This event is organized by the S.H. Ho Urology Centre of CUHK, providing free Prostate-Specific Antigen (PSA) testing services for eligible individuals.
Event Venue: Shatin District (the exact address will be provided after successful registration)
Event Details: (Estimated duration: about one hour)
Video Presentation: An easy-to-understand introduction to the examination and treatment of prostate cancer and benign prostatic hyperplasia
Prostate Screening: Eligible participants will receive one free Prostate-Specific Antigen (PSA) test.
Testing Method: We will collect blood samples from participants via a fingertip blood test and conduct an on-site PSA test using a PSA testing device. Results will be available in about ten minutes.
Eligibility:
Gender: Male
Age: 50-75 years old
Have never undergone any prostate-related examination
If you are interested in participating, please fill in the online form below;
https://forms.office.com/r/HRJspBWSW6
For more information about the assessment of prostate cancer risk, please visit the following website:
https://urologycentre.com.hk/zh-hant/diseases/detail/how-to-investigate-and-make-diagnosis-for-prostate-cancer
All information provided by participants will be kept confidential. For any enquiries, please contact us (WhatsApp: 5160 6904; Email: yellowwong@cuhk.edu.hk)
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

title: ”Forest of Books, Phoenix in Flight: The Art and Life of Ye Lingfeng” Exhibition Talk 2 「藝林擷葉 靈鳳于飛：葉靈鳳的美術與人生」展覽講座（二）
bodyText:

Events / Activities
”Forest of Books, Phoenix in Flight: The Art and Life of Ye Lingfeng” Exhibition Talk 2 「藝林擷葉 靈鳳于飛：葉靈鳳的美術與人生」展覽講座（二） - CUHK Library
From: The Chinese University of Hong Kong Library
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
spc@lib.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
日期：2026年7月31日（星期五）
時間：下午3時至5時
地點：香港中文大學圖書館地下數碼學術研究室
主持：香港中文大學中國語言及文學系高級講師張詠梅博士
語言：粵語
講題一：「故紙堆裡覓靈鳳」
講者多年潛心蒐藏葉靈鳳相關珍稀書籍與文獻，涵蓋早期初版典籍、舊時報刊、親筆手跡、藏書票及往來書札等罕見珍貴藏品。憑藉這些獨特史料，立體還原葉靈鳳跌宕豐實的人生履跡與深厚文學造詣，回溯這位南來文人落籍香江、深耕香港文壇的耕耘歲月，系統梳理其於本土文學建設、地方掌故研究方面的突出貢獻，全面闡釋其在中、港兩地文脈傳承之中，留下的深遠價值與不可磨滅的歷史貢獻。
講者：吳邦謀先生為資深特許電力工程師，現擔任張愛玲會會長、香港收藏家協會高級副會長。其學術研究深耕張愛玲、葉靈鳳兩大名家，同時涉獵香港航空史領域，研究視角獨特且積澱深厚。吳先生迄今已出版專著十部，代表作有《葉靈鳳百二年》、《張愛玲在香港》、《尋覓張愛玲》、《從啟德至赤鱲角》、《香港航空 125 年》等，於2015年榮獲第二屆香港金閱奬之「最佳書籍奬」，為香港文學研究與本土歷史研究，累積豐厚的文獻與學術價值。
講題二：「葉靈鳳的五個美學面孔」
葉靈鳳（1905–1975）以文名世，卻同時是一位被低估的視覺藝術實踐者。本講以五個美學面孔切入——頹美夢想者、表現主義者、視覺預言者、浪漫主義者、文藝鑑賞者——追蹤葉氏從上海到香港的視覺足跡：書刊封面、插畫、藏書票與印刷品收藏，及其與比亞茲萊、蕗谷虹兒、麥綏萊勒等人的美學對話。「美術家葉靈鳳」，是另一個值得正視的文學史人物。
講者：黃念欣，香港中文大學中國語言及文學系副教授、香港文學研究中心主任、文學院副院長（公關及推廣）、專研香港文學及書目檔案，著有《晚期風格︰香港女作家三論》、《起初如何︰香港文學十論》、散文集《夕拾朝花》、《熱風》。
講座報名：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13735742
*本館將於活動中拍照或錄影以作紀錄及展示。參與此活動即代表允許「香港中文大學圖書館」所拍攝的相片或影像作公開展示或宣傳用途。

葉靈鳳（1905–1975）以文名世，卻同時是一位被低估的視覺藝術實踐者。本講以五個美學面孔切入——頹美夢想者、表現主義者、視覺預言者、浪漫主義者、文藝鑑賞者——追蹤葉氏從上海到香港的視覺足跡：書刊封面、插畫、藏書票與印刷品收藏，及其與比亞茲萊、蕗谷虹兒、麥綏萊勒等人的美學對話。「美術家葉靈鳳」，是另一個值得正視的文學史人物。
講者：黃念欣，香港中文大學中國語言及文學系副教授、香港文學研究中心主任、文學院副院長（公關及推廣）、專研香港文學及書目檔案，著有《晚期風格︰香港女作家三論》、《起初如何︰香港文學十論》、散文集《夕拾朝花》、《熱風》。

title: Public Lecture by Professor Wing Hong Chan on "The Liquidity Paradox: Geopolitical Risk and De-dollarization", 11 August (Tue), 11:00 am
bodyText:

Public Lecture by Professor Wing Hong Chan on "The Liquidity Paradox: Geopolitical Risk and De-dollarization", 11 August (Tue), 11:00 am  - Lau Chor Tak Institute of Global Economics and Finance
From: Rachel Lee
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
igef@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Speaker:   Professor Wing Hong Chan
Professor, Wilfrid Laurier University
Date:         11 August 2026 (Tuesday)
Time:         11:00 am – 12:15 pm
Venue:       Room 301, 3/F, Wu Ho Man Yuen Building,
The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Language: English
Abstract:
This paper investigates the disconnect between the growing political narrative of de-dollarization and the continued empirical dominance of the U.S. dollar. We propose a “Liquidity Paradox” framework to reconcile this divergence by distinguishing between short-term tactical asset substitution and long-term strategic diversification. Using a monthly panel of 11 major emerging market economies from 2011 to 2023, we document three key findings.
First, contrary to the flight-to-gold hypothesis, geopolitical shocks induce a short-run flight-to-dollar effect, particularly among financially constrained economies facing liquidity pressures. Second, we identify a “Sanction Paradox”: since the 2014 Crimea crisis, non-allied countries have increased their reliance on dollar reserves as a precaution against potential financial exclusion. Third, although there is clear evidence of a post-2018 trend toward currency diversification, this strategic shift is offset by re-concentration driven by persistent geopolitical risk.
Overall, we show that geopolitical instability paradoxically reinforces the dollar’s role as the dominant safe-haven asset, making de-dollarization a constrained and self-limiting process.
About the Speaker:
Professor Wing Hong Chan is an econometrician working at the intersection of financial economics and forecasting methods to investigate financial markets' efficiency. Professor Chan received a BA (1995) from the University of Manitoba and a Ph.D. (2002) from the University of Alberta. He taught at City University Hong Kong beginning in 2006 before returning to Wilfrid Laurier University in 2009. His research interests center around modelling and forecasting volatility and economic risks. His articles have been published in the
Journal of Business and Economic Statistics, Journal of Futures Markets, Oxford Bulletin of Economics and Statistics, and Resources and Energy Economics
, among other journals.

Dear students,
【
Call for Student Volunteers
】
Opportunities for the Elderly Project 2026 - Piecing Together Inner Voices: A Story Collection
During the new academic year, do you ever find yourself wishing for a break from the usual routine of lectures and campus life? The Salvation Army Nam Tai Centre for Senior Citizens is now recruiting student volunteers to join "Piecing Together Inner Voices: A Story Collection". We invite empathetic students like you to become dedicated listeners for the elderly and their carers.
"Piecing Together Inner Voices: A Story Collection" aims to help carers document their caregiving journeys and share these personal stories with the public through online platforms and community media. The programme offers young volunteers a meaningful opportunity to learn empathy through active listening, while empowering the elderly to regain a sense of purpose and self‑worth through storytelling. Join us in making a difference together. Let's create a community of care and connection!

bodyText:

Announcements
🗣️👉[Earn $100!] Recruiting Ethnic Chinese / Pakistani Hong Kong Long-term Residents / Pakistani non-Hong Kong Residents for an Online Interview💡 (1 hour)  - Department of English
From: Prof. Wilkinson Daniel Wong Gonzales
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
wdwonggonzales@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
💡Earn $100 for an online interview! You are invited to participate in a study on accent description led by Prof. Wilkinson Daniel Wong Gonzales from the Department of English, CUHK. The interview will take approximately 45 - 60 minutes.
Seats are limited. Participation will be confirmed on a first come, first served basis.
Research Purpose:
- To investigate how listeners arrive at judgements concerning how linguistic variables independently convey social meaning.
Eligibility:
- Ethnic Chinese Hong Kong Long-term Residents (who have been living in Hong Kong for at least 7 years); OR
- Ethnic Pakistani Hong Kong Long-term Residents (who have been living in Hong Kong for at least 7 years)
To Participate:
If you are interested, please submit a short response form via the link below:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_b8CVmGWLLNypx2K
Compensation:
You will receive HKD100 as remuneration for participation
.
Confidentiality and Consent:
All responses will be kept strictly confidential. You will be asked to provide your name, email address, and an optional alias. These are collected only for administrative purposes (e.g., tracking participation). You may withdraw from the study at any time without penalty.
Ethics Approval:
SBRE-25-0095 “Revisiting the Hong Kong English accent: How micro-variation, awareness, and context shape its social life and meanings”
Enquiry:
Prof. Wilkinson Daniel Wong Gonzales (wdwonggonzales@cuhk.edu.hk)

bodyText:

Announcements
💥👩🏻🧑🏻👨🏻 Recruiting Age ≥18 Hong Kong Native Cantonese Speakers for a Cantonese-English Bilingual Experiment [💰HKD230 Compensation Upon Completion] 招募18歲或以上香港粵語母語使用者參與粵英雙語實驗👵🏻🧓🏻👴🏻 💥【完成實驗可獲💰HKD230報酬】  - Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages
From: Miko NG Hoi Tung
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
hoitungng@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
The Department of Linguistics at the Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently recruiting participants who meet the following criteria for a study on Hong Kong Cantonese-English bilingualism. The study is led by Xiaotian Wang, a PhD student at Harvard University, and Professor Kathryn Franich.
Participants need to be:
- From Hong Kong
- Proficient in both Cantonese and English (capable of daily communication in both languages)
- At least 18 years old
- Has unimpaired (or corrected) vision, with no severe eye discomfort
- Has no hearing impairments
- Has no language, hearing, or neurological impairments
- Has no speech impediments
- Willing to be audio recorded
Procedure: You will listen to several Cantonese audio recordings and provide responses. The entire experiment lasts approximately 2 hours.
Location: CUHK Leung Kau Kui Building G/F
Period: July 2026
Compensation: HK$230 (depending on the actual duration of the experiment)
If you meet the recruitment criteria above and are interested in participating, please fill out the registration form below. Our researchers will contact you as soon as possible:
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeD21YEYJeoffCzOQSG0MN-NtTUzy6LN0-wq1FtMxUjb814nA/viewform?usp=sharing&ouid=110803938824956659314
All personally identifiable information provided during your participation will be kept strictly confidential.
If you have any enquiry, please feel free to contact Research Assistant Ms. Wang at
xiaotianwang@g.harvard.edu
.
香港中文大學語言學系正就一項由哈佛大學博士生Xiaotian Wang和Kathryn Franich教授主理的香港粵語與英語雙語研究招募符合以下條件的受試者：
- 來自香港
- 能夠熟練使用粵語和英語（兩種語言均可進行日常交流）-
- 年滿18周歲
- 視力（矯正後）正常，無嚴重眼部不適
- 聽力正常
- 無語言、聽力或神經系統相關疾病
- 無言語障礙
- 願意進行語音錄音
實驗內容：你將獲邀參與一項粵語語音實驗，聆聽若干粵語錄音並作出回應。實驗時長約2小時。
地點：香港中文大學梁銶琚樓G層
時間：2026年7月
報酬：HK$230（視實驗時長而定）
如滿足上述招募條件且有興趣參與，請填妥下方報名表格，我們的研究人員會儘快聯絡你：
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeD21YEYJeoffCzOQSG0MN-NtTUzy6LN0-wq1FtMxUjb814nA/viewform?usp=sharing&ouid=110803938824956659314
有關你參與實驗所提供的所有可識別個人身份的信息將被嚴格保密。
如對本項實驗有任何疑問題，歡迎聯絡研究助理王小姐（
xiaotianwang@g.harvard.edu
）。

title: 【💰💰💰$200 Coupon💰💰💰】Recruiting Children (aged 4 or under) for the Gut Microbiome and At-risk Children's Brain Development Study🦠💩🧠📝 誠意邀請5歲以下兒童參加腸道微生態與兒童大腦發展及風險研究
bodyText:

Announcements
【💰💰💰$200 Coupon💰💰💰】Recruiting Children (aged 4 or under) for the Gut Microbiome and At-risk Children's Brain Development Study🦠💩🧠📝 誠意邀請5歲以下兒童參加腸道微生態與兒童大腦發展及風險研究 - Department of Psychiatry
From: Dr. WONG Wing Ho, Oscar
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
hatch@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
家長您好，我們是香港中文大學醫學院精神科學系的研究團隊。本研究由香港中文大學醫學院精神科學系、內科及藥物治療學系統籌。
本研究團隊誠邀5歲以下兒童參與一項有關腸道微生態與兒童大腦發展及風險研究。此研究希望透過收集小朋友之大便及口腔樣本，幫助了解腸道微生態與大腦發展的關係。
研究對象:
1) 確診/懷疑小朋友有自閉症傾向或其他發展問題
2) 4歲或以下的小朋友 (交齊問卷和樣本的日子未滿5歲即可)
3) 父母皆為華裔或亞裔人士
4) 小朋友18歲以下的兄弟姊妹
以下為是次研究需要完成的事項：
1) 簽署參加同意書🖋️
2) 網上問卷調查🖥️：網上問卷主要詢問小朋友的行為及腸道情況，填寫時間約45分鐘
3) 收集大便和口腔樣本🧪：我們會給家長一個樣本收集包，請家長使用收集包內的物在家中資協助收集樣本
4) 飲食習慣的問卷📄：記錄小朋友的飲食習慣
完成研究後，參加者可以獲得$200的超市現金券、 G-NiiB益生菌試用裝和腸道健康報告作為答謝🧧 另外，家長有機會被邀請進行面談並隨訪2年,如有需要我們會提供轉介信。是次研究是自願參與性質參與，這個研究期間所取得的資料都會被嚴格保密。
如家長有意願參與此項研究，請填寫以下網上篩選問卷(https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_81kdBVoLu4f6l3o)。收到問卷回覆後，我們會再與合適參加是次研究的小朋友之家長連絡。
如果家長對研究細節有任何疑問，歡迎透過WhatsApp 6099-3064或致電 2607-6057與我們聯絡。
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Dear Parents,
We are a team of researchers from the Department of Psychiatry at the Chinese University of Hong Kong. We are conducting a research project jointly organised by the Department of Psychiatry, the Department of Medicine and Therapeutics of the Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Our team sincerely invites your children to participate in research on gut microbiome and children's brain development. Through collecting stool and buccal samples, we aim to investigate the relationship between gut microbiome and brain development.
A gut health report will be provided, A G-Niib probiotics trial pack and a $200 supermarket voucher will be awarded to participants.
Target participants:
1) The child is diagnosed/suspected to have autism or other developmental problems
2) The child is 4 years old or under (all questionnaires and samples are submitted before 5 years old)
3) Both parents are Chinese or Asian
4) Children’s brothers and sisters under 18 years old are also welcome to join
Procedures and details of this Study:
1) Research Consent🖋️
2) Online Questionnaire 🖥️: A 45-minute questionnaire on children’s behaviors and their physical health condition
3) Stool and Buccal Sample Collection🧪: Samples collection kit will be provided for sample collection at home
4) Dietary Questionnaire📄: Recording children's eating habits
You will receive a $200 supermarket voucher after completing all the research procedures🧧. Participation is voluntary, and your responses will be kept confidential. The information you provide will be used solely for research purposes.
If you are interested in participating in our research study, please fill out the following online questionnaire (https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_81kdBVoLu4f6l3o). We will contact you afterwards if your children are suitable to join this study.
For inquiries, please contact 2607-6057 or WhatsApp 6099-3064.

From: Tim Lau
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
timlau@surgery.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學泌尿外科研究招募
:
香港中文大學泌尿外科現正進行一項男性特定群體的尿液及生物樣本HPV和病例對照研究。人類乳頭瘤病毒（HPV） 是全球最常見的性傳染病毒之一，能影響男性並導致多種疾病，包括生殖器疣（椰菜花）、陰莖癌、肛門癌 及 口咽癌。然而，男性 HPV 的感染情況一直缺乏研究，而你的參與將有助填補這個重要的知識空白。
本研究旨在了解HPV感染率、患者人口統計特徵、臨床特徵以及被診斷患有HPV相關惡性腫瘤的男性患者的疾病負擔。以評估男性尿液 HPV 測試的準確性，並更深入了解男性感染 HPV的風險因素，以及幫助未來預防及治療策略。
-如初步檢測確診為HPV陽性的患者，或將安排進一步行檢查 (例如:軟式膀胱鏡檢查等等)及跟進複檢。
參加者條件（男性，18歲或以上）：
1) 陰莖癌，肛⾨癌，或咽喉癌患者
2) 曾患性傳染病
3) 曾有同性性⾏為
4) 慢性前列腺炎患者
地點：沙⽥威爾斯親王醫院
樣本收集： 尿液及尿道拭子、口咽拭子、肛門拭子、冠狀溝拭子
-填寫簡單問卷
-根據情況也可能採集 20 毫升血液
[費用全免]
-完成整個研究計劃後可獲得港幣
$400
津貼

所收集的資料僅用於學術研究用途
名額有限，先到先得!
閣下如對本研究有興趣請透過以下連結報名：
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSf__iQ0Ike8hpG6qIm1mjtF0nCTdcPFKT2v9jFARsuZbqjMJw/viewform?usp=header
-如果評估合適參與研究，將稍後聯絡你，謝謝
如有查詢，歡迎電郵: timlau@surgery.cuhk.edu.hk，與研究人員劉先生聯絡。

Free HPV Screening for Men in Specific Groups [Free!!]
The Chinese University of Hong Kong Division of Urology Research Recruitment
The Department of Surgery (Urology), The Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently recruiting participants for a hybrid cohort and case-control study on male urinary HPV.
Human Papillomavirus (HPV) is one of the most common sexually transmitted viruses worldwide. It can affect men and lead to serious conditions including genital warts, penile cancer, anal cancer, and oropharyngeal cancer. However, HPV infection in men remains under-studied. Your cooperation is highly solicited.
This research aims to determine HPV prevalence, patient demographics, clinical characteristics, and disease burden in men. It will also evaluate the accuracy of a new urine-based HPV DNA test and explore risk factors to support future prevention and treatment strategies.
Participants who test positive for HPV in the initial urine test may be invited for further investigations (e.g. flexible cystoscopy) and regular follow-up re-testing.
Eligibility (Males aged 18 or above)
Patients diagnosed with penile cancer, anal cancer, or oropharyngeal cancer
Men with a history of sexually transmitted diseases (STD)
Men who have sex with men (MSM)
Patients with chronic prostatitis / chronic pelvic pain syndrome (CPPS)
Study Location: Prince of Wales Hospital, Sha Tin
Narrative description
Urine sample + swabs (urethral, oropharyngeal, anal, coronal sulcus)
Complete a simple questionnaire
Optional: 20 ml blood sample (if required)
Free of Charge in HPV test !!
Upon successful completion of the study, participants will receive a
HKD 400
travel subsidy
Your Privacy is Fully Protected.
Data will only be used for academic research purposes.
If you are interested, please register via the link below:
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSf__iQ0Ike8hpG6qIm1mjtF0nCTdcPFKT2v9jFARsuZbqjMJw/viewform?usp=header
Suitable applicants will be contacted shortly.
For inquiries, please email:  timlau@surgery.cuhk.edu.hk

https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

香港中文大學內科及藥物治療學系與香港中文大學香港中西醫結合醫學研究所現正聯合進行一項為期36週，以內服中藥(沖劑)治療 2 型糖尿病人
🙋 研究對象：18至70歲華人
沒有重大疾病，沒有服用中藥， 身體質量指數 (BMI) ≥18 kg/m²  (公斤 ÷ 米 ÷ 米)
不吸煙或已戒煙至少 12 個月，如女性目前未懷孕
患糖尿病未滿 6 年，且在過去 3 個月內未使用任何降血糖藥物（包括胰島素）治療
至少具備以下其中一項風險因素:
糖尿病家族史 (尤其父母或兄弟姐妹在40歲前診斷 )
代謝綜合症 (3高：高血糖，高血壓，高膽固醇)
超重或肥胖
脂肪肝
多囊卵巢綜合症
妊娠糖尿病病史
如不確定自己是否患有糖尿病，會安排你服用葡萄糖飲料（75 克口服葡萄糖耐量試驗）

[Clinical safety, efficacy and multiomic evaluation of a novel Chinese Medicine formula in Type 2 diabetes: Effects on beta-cell function and insulin resistance
.]
Department of Medicine and Therapeutics and Hong Kong Institute of Integrative Medicine, CUHK are jointly conducting a 36-week clinical study on the use of oral traditional Chinese medicine (granule form) for treating type 2 diabetes.
🙋 Eligibility Criteria: Ethnic Chinese individuals aged 18 to 70 years
No major illnesses, not currently taking any traditional Chinese medicine, and with a Body Mass Index (BMI) ≥ 18 kg/m² (kg ÷ metre ÷ metre)
Non-smokers or those who have quit smoking for at least 12 months; females must not be currently pregnant
Diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for less than 6 years and have not used any glucose-lowering medications (including insulin) in the past 3 months
Must have at least one of the following risk factors:
Family history of diabetes (especially if parents or siblings were diagnosed before age of 40)
Metabolic syndrome (three highs: high blood sugar, high blood pressure, high blood cholesterol)
Overweight or obesity
Fatty liver
Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
History of gestational diabetes
If you are unsure whether you have diabetes, a 75g oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) will be arranged for you.
📋
Study Procedures Include:
Chinese and Western medical assessments, Electrocardiogram (ECG), Liver fibrosis scan, Blood tests, Questionnaire completion, Taking either the study Chinese medicine or a placebo
🏥 Location: Ward 3M, 3/F, Old Block, Diabetes and Endocrinology Research Centre, Prince of Wales Hospital, Sha Tin, New Territories
Free of charge to participate.
Successful participants may receive an allowance of up to HKD $1,000.
Limited quota – first come, first served!
Register via the following link:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/mycuform/view.php?id=3542692
If you are eligible based on initial assessment, our research team will contact you shortly. Thank you! 🙏🏻

📞 3505 3897 / 6937 3365

Announcements
Recruiting vocally healthy participants aged 18 and above to participate in an acoustic analysis study to explore the quality and characteristics of the voice (HK$150 coupon) 誠意邀請18歲或以上沒有聲線障礙的人士參與探索聲線質量和特徵的聲學分析研究 (HK$150 coupon) - Department of Otorhinolarynogology, Head and Neck Surgery
From: Rina To
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
rinato@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學耳鼻咽喉 頭頸外科學系現正招募十八歲或以上沒有聲線障礙的人士參與一項聲學分析的研究，旨在探究平滑化倒頻譜突出峰值 (CPPS) 的臨界值和其診斷準確性。
CPPS是一種可應用於日常對話的聲線聲學分析參數。CPPS相對於其他常用的聲學參數具有更高的診斷準確性。但是，根據文獻的報告顯示，使用不同的語言，聲線樣本類型，和軟件，都會影響到CPPS的結果。我們希望這項研究的結果能夠為臨床醫生和研究人員對聲線障礙患者進行客觀測量並為聲線評估的量化結果提供明確的參考。
招募對象：
年滿十八歲或以上
沒有聲線問題的人士
以廣東話為母語
費用：
全免
評估與檢查地點：
威爾斯親王醫院
研究程序及内容：
1）參加者將填寫聲線問卷， 並親臨威爾斯親王醫院接受喉纖維內視鏡檢查和聲線錄製。
2）喉纖維內視鏡檢查時能清楚看見咽喉，每次檢查需時約三十分鐘，是屬於低風險的檢查，一般只會感到輕微不適。
報名連結﹕
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/mycuform/view.php?id=4267989
參與研究，獲得獎勵：
完成聲線評估後，您可獲得港幣150元的超市現金券。
名額有限，先到先得。收到報名後，我們會再與合資格的參加者聯絡。
歡迎將此招募信息推薦給身邊有需要的家人以及朋友。
如有查詢，請與研究人員王先生（Mr. Wang）聯絡。
電郵：
zikaiwang@link.cuhk.edu.hk
The Department of Otorhinolaryngology, Head and Neck Surgery, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, is currently recruiting vocally healthy participants aged 18 and above for a study investigating the cut-off score and diagnostic accuracy of the smoothed cepstral peak prominence (CPPS) for Cantonese speakers with dysphonia.
CPPS is a parameter for acoustic analysis of voice that can be used in everyday conversation to provide a more comprehensive and realistic picture of an individual's vocal characteristics in natural communication situations. CPPS has a higher diagnostic accuracy than other commonly used acoustic parameters. However, reports in the literature indicate that the use of different languages, different types of voice samples, and different software can affect the results of the CPPS. We hope that the results of this study will provide clinicians and researchers with a clear reference for the quantitative results of objective measurement and voice assessment in patients with voice disorders.
Recruitment target:
Age 18 or above
People who do not have voice problems
Fluent in Cantonese as a native language or proficient in Cantonese
Cost:
Free of charge
Location:
Prince of Wales Hospital
Procedures and details of this Study:
Participants will undergo a laryngeal videostroboscopy examination and a comprehensive voice assessment at Prince of Wales Hospital.
A videostroboscopy examination can clearly observe the throat to detect whether it has structural or functional problem for speaking. Each examination takes approximately thirty minutes. It is a low-risk procedure, and participants typically only experience mild discomfort.
Registration link:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/mycuform/view.php?id=4267989
Participate in the study and receive a reward:
After completing the voice assessment, you will receive a HK$ 150 supermarket gift card.
Limited seats available on a first-come first-served basis. We will contact you afterwards if you are suitable to join this study.
Welcome to recommend this recruitment information to your family and friends in need.
If you have any inquiries, please contact Mr. Wang.
Email: zikaiwang@link.cuhk.edu.hk
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

From: Lyon You

Registration is invited for the following academic seminar scheduled for
16 July (Thur) from 3pm to 6pm at the JC School of Public Health and Primary Care
.  Topics of sharing will centre around how
"One Health" research and initiatives would empower public health
.
A keynote speech will be given by Prof. George F. Gao
, Fellow of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) and a Professor at the Institute of Microbiology of CAS.
The seminar will be conducted
mainly in Putonghua.
Registration is free, and all are welcome.  Your support and participation would be greatly appreciated.
Registration Link
:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13735842
Please find more details in Chinese below.
香港中文大學醫學院賽馬會公共衞生與基層醫療學院十分榮幸能夠邀請中國科學院院士高福院士、香港中文大學（深圳）醫學院于廣軍副院長及深圳市兒童醫院麻曉鵬主任醫師，於
2026年7月16日（星期四）
蒞臨本學院出席主題爲
「同一健康行動：環境可持續性與跨領域研究賦能公共衞生」
的研討會，並與本學院學者交流。
「同一健康（One Health）」理念強調人類、動物健康與環境生態可持續發展之間存在緊密而互為依賴的連結。是次研討會匯聚多位學者和專家，從跨地域管治策略、環境科學、醫學人工智能、醫療創新實踐等多個角度，分享研究成果與經驗，探討跨領域行動怎樣賦能公共衞生，應對群體健康的挑戰。研討會主要以普通話進行，部分環節將使用英語。
學院現誠邀您報名參與研討會，一同探索「同一健康」的前沿發展，攜手推動公共衞生的可持續未來。
請透過此鏈接登記報名
：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13735842
。報名將於2026年7月14日（星期二）下午2時截止。
活動詳情：
日期：2026年7月16日（星期四）
時間：下午3時至6時
地點：沙田威爾斯親王醫院公共衞生學院大樓1樓繼昌堂資訊中心（KCTCRC）
語言：普通話（部分環節*以英語進行）

歡迎致辭
黃仰山教授
香港中文大學醫學院賽馬會公共衞生及基層醫療學院院長
同一健康：從公共衞生到全球健康

Registration Begins

CUHK Chinese Medicine Clinics (CUSCM Clinics) will provide Tianjiu Therapy from July to August 2026. Interested parties are welcome to register through our website and hotline. Tianjiu Therapy is conducted during San Fu Tian when Yang Qi is strong, which is one of the hottest periods of the year according to the 24 Solar Terms. By applying the warm-natured herbal patches on certain acupoints, it stimulates the body to regulate the meridian system and improve the immunity, based on the principles of ‘Cultivating Yang-Energy in Spring and Summer’ (春夏養陽) and ‘Preventing Winter-Occurring Diseases in Summer’ (冬病夏防). Tianjiu Therapy is suitable for individuals with cold syndrome of allergic rhinitis, asthma, stomach pain, diarrhea, dysmenorrhea, cold (recurrent) etc. Portable Chinese Medicine Herbal Sachets are also available for purchase at HK$33 each for suitable participants.
